Exceptional Educators. Inclusive Education. Nurturing Community.

Key Information & Policies
Curriculum Overview
Secondary Phase
At Prendergast Vale School, we believe that all students, regardless of their starting points, should have access to a broad curriculum that prepares them to become successful learners, who can make a positive contribution to society. Our aim is for every student who leaves this school at age 16 to be on the pathway to university, leading to successful careers with good prospects. Students will be exposed to a range of learning opportunities designed to develop their knowledge, skills and understanding through the subjects they learn inside the classroom and the enrichment opportunities we provide outside the classroom, to cultivate their cultural capital. The curriculum at Prendergast Vale School, will allow them to achieve academic excellence as well as build their characters to ensure they grow into resilient, confident and optimistic individuals that are able to adapt to the challenges of the 21st century.
All students study the following subjects at Key Stage 3: Maths, English, Science, Computer Science, Music, PE, Art, Design and Technology, Spanish, History, Geography and Religious Education.
At Key stage 4, all students study the following Core Curriculum leading to a GCSE qualification in the following subjects: Maths, English Literature, English Language, Biology, Chemistry, Physics (Combined Science with some students studying Separate Science), Spanish and a Humanities subject (History or Geography).
Students then elect to study a further two subjects from this list: Computer Science, Food Technology, Music, PE, Art, Design and Technology, a second Humanities subject (History or Geography), Drama and RE.
See the Year Group curriculum booklets below for further details.
This is in addition to their statutory participation in studies which support their wider development in sports, ICT and social, moral, spiritual and cultural studies.
If you would like more information, please email admin@prendergast-vale.com

Admission Appeals for Starting School 2026 (Reception)
This provides the Key Dates and other arrangements for hearing appeals for The Leathersellers’ Federation of Schools, including Prendergast Vale School, for 2026-27.
The deadline for lodging a Starting School (Reception) appeal to this school is 15 May 2026.
Appeals arrangements are set out in accordance with the Schools Admission Appeals Code (2021). Appeals will be conducted remotely as virtual hearings. If an appellant does not have online access, alternative arrangements may be discussed with the clerk. The admission authority and clerk will respond to any further advice and guidance as necessary.
Appeals arrangements 2026
Under the School Standards & Framework Act 1998, the Academy Trust of Academy Schools has to make appeal arrangements for parents/carers who wish to appeal a decision not to offer a child a place at the school.

Maths
Intent: Our Vision for Every Pupil
At Prendergast Vale, we ignite a passion for mathematics through an ambitious, interconnected curriculum tailored for every learner. We don’t just teach procedures; we cultivate mathematical thinkers who possess the fluency to calculate, the reason to justify, and the resilience to tackle the unknown.
We empower our pupils to be:
Visualisers: Harnessing the Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract (CPA) journey to turn complexity into clarity and build unshakable conceptual foundations.
Describers: Mastering mathematical language allows our pupils to move beyond "getting the answer" to articulating the why behind the way.
Experimenters: By identifying patterns and weaving links across the curriculum, our pupils see maths not as a list of topics, but as a universal language of discovery.
Implementation: Mathematics in Action
Our curriculum is delivered through the White Rose Maths Scheme which is a mastery-led approach, ensuring that concepts are explored in depth rather than rushed through. We translate our intent into the classroom through three specific pedagogical strands:
The Visualisation Strategy (CPA)
We ensure that every new concept is introduced through a physical or visual lens before moving to abstract symbols.
Concrete: Pupils use physical manipulatives to "feel" the mathematics.
Pictorial: Pupils use visual models (like the Bar Model) to bridge the gap between objects and numbers.
Abstract: Once the concept is "seen," we move to formal written methods, ensuring symbols are grounded in reality.
Mathematical Oracy
A Prendergast Vale classroom is a "talk-rich" environment where mathematical language is treated as a core literacy skill.
Sentence Stems: We provide scaffolds to help pupils articulate their reasoning.
Precision Vocabulary: Key mathematical vocabulary is introduced and used consistently by staff and pupils.
Justification: Children are encouraged to explain their thinking.
Reasoning & Problem Solving
We move beyond rote learning by embedding "low threshold, high ceiling" tasks that allow every child to explore.
Pattern Seeking: Curiosity is encouraged and opportunities to find patterns are given to demystify the maths
Productive Struggle: We celebrate "wrong" answers as vital data points and provide non-routine problems that require testing hypotheses.
Impact: Measuring Success
The impact of our curriculum is that pupils leave us as mathematically literate individuals capable of navigating the modern world. We measure this through:
Mathematical Mastery: Pupils demonstrate deep, long-term understanding, evidenced by their ability to apply skills across different contexts.
Articulate Reasoning: Through book looks and pupil voice, pupils demonstrate they can use precise vocabulary to justify their thinking.
Resilience & Confidence: Pupils show a "can-do" attitude toward challenge. They do not give up when faced with unfamiliar problems; they experiment and pivot.
Consistent Achievement: Pupils meet and exceed age-related expectations, with the gap narrowing between different learner groups due to our inclusive, high-aspiration approach.

EYFS Curriculum
In the Early Years Foundation Stage at Prendergast Vale we aim to provide a memorable and inclusive curriculum which gives children not only a broad understanding of the world they live in but the social skills to interact within it.
We firmly believe that all children deserve the very best opportunities that education has to offer so whilst children are in Nursery and Reception class we want to ensure that all children achieve to their full potential regardless of any barriers to learning. We want children to be effective communicators and collaborative learners; taking risks with the resilience to make mistakes and reflect and learn from them.
We empower our children to be critical thinkers and independent learners through play based learning and small group activities that respond to the children’s interests. We intend that the children leave the EYFS phase having developed the skills, knowledge and desire to begin their journey of being life-long learners as they progress to the next stage of their education as our school motto says ‘in perpetuum discimus’ - we are forever learning.

Curriculum Information
Our Primary Vision: Forever Learning
In the Primary phase at Prendergast Vale, we provide a memorable and inclusive curriculum that does more than just teach; it inspires. We want our children to develop a deep understanding of the world around them alongside the social confidence to navigate it.
We firmly believe that every child deserves the very best start in life. Our dedicated team strives to help every pupil reach their full potential, ensuring that barriers to learning are overcome through tailored support and high expectations.
Growing Brave, Independent Learners
We want our pupils to be effective communicators and collaborative partners. By creating a "no-fear" classroom culture, we encourage children to take risks and show resilience. We teach them that mistakes aren't failures—they are essential steps in reflecting and growing. We use ‘struggle time’ to ensure children develop the resilience they need to become increasingly more independent.
Our "spaced curriculum" is carefully sequenced to ensure children revisit key themes, allowing their knowledge to stick and their curiosity to grow.
‘In Perpetuum Discimus’ – We are Forever Learning
We live our school motto every day. We develop life-long learners through:
An Aspirational Culture: We celebrate high achievement and encourage every child to aim high.
Restorative Practice: Our behaviour approach is rooted in dialogue and mutual respect, teaching children how to resolve conflicts and communicate kindly.
Small-Step Progress: Lessons are broken down into manageable "small steps" to ensure no child is left behind and everyone feels a sense of daily success.
Targeted Support: We use regular progress reviews to catch gaps early, ensuring that intervention is quick, effective, and meaningful.
Learning Behaviours: which are - Collaborative, Imaginative, Persistent, Curious and Disciplined.
Foundations for the Future
By the end of Year 6, our aim children leave the Primary phase as reflective, curious thinkers with a genuine passion for discovery. They move on to our Secondary phase with the firm foundations, independent study skills, and academic confidence they need to thrive in the next stage of their journey.
